                                      PROJECT NO. 58000

      EVALUATION OF                                 §            BEFORE THE
       TRANSMISSION                                 §     PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
      COST RECOVERY                                 §             OF TEXAS


 COMMENTS OF EROCK ON JULY 10 PFP RE: EVALUATION OF TRANSMISSION
                        COST RECOVERY

       ERock appreciates the careful consideration being given to review existing methodology
used to charge wholesale transmission costs to distribution providers under Public Utility
Regulatory Act (PURA) §35.004(d).
       ERock is a Houston-based microgrid owner, operator, and developer with over 350 dual-
purpose microgrids in operation throughout Texas, providing over 560 MW of gas-fired,
dispatchable capacity to the grid. ERock is also operational in states across the country in support
of critical facilities and large loads. ERock encourages the Commission to consider the following
responses to Commission recommendations regarding the evaluation of transmission cost
recovery.


GENERAL COMMENTS
       ERock supports GRIT’s comments and recommendations in this proceeding, including its
emphasis on cost causation principles, recognition of enforceable load flexibility in both planning
and billing, and preservation of incentives for customers to reduce actual grid withdrawal during
coincident peaks. ERock also supports GRIT’s recommendation that large load obligations reflect
demonstrated system impacts and the level of firm service required, rather than relying solely on
customer classification or contracted demand. With respect to the proposed 12CP methodology,
ERock offers the following additional recommendation regarding the relative weighting of
monthly peaks.
       ERock recommends that, if the Commission adopts a 12CP methodology, it
considers weighting summer and winter coincident peaks more heavily than spring and fall peaks.
A uniform weighting treats every monthly peak as equally relevant to transmission cost causation,
even though the conditions that place the greatest demands on the ERCOT system are more
concentrated in particular seasons. A methodology that assigns greater weight to summer and

                                            Page 1 of 3
 winter peaks would better preserve the price signal for customers to reduce demand during periods
when system conditions are most likely to be stressed.
       ERock recommends that ERCOT develop seasonal weights using transparent, multi-year
data, including the distribution of ERCOT’s total peak load and net load hours by month, the
frequency of significant transmission constraints, the extent to which each monthly peak
contributes to identified transmission projects, and planned generation and transmission outages.
The Commission should periodically review the weights as the ERCOT system changes. A
weighted 12CP structure would address the Commission’s broader year round peak framework
without diluting the strongest incentives to reduce demand during the conditions most likely to
drive transmission investment.




CONCLUSION
       ERock appreciates the opportunity to submit these responses to Commission Staff’s
recommendations on transmission cost recovery. As the Commission continues to move forward
with Project No. 58000 and related efforts, ERock is committed to supporting the effort to ensure
improved grid reliability, resiliency, and stability.


                                                        Respectfully submitted,

                                                        /s/ Monica Batra-Shrader
                                                        Monica Batra-Shrader
                                                        Policy Manager, Central Region
                                                        ERock
                                                        mbatra@erock.com
